A practice unit, preseason start, projected minutes and regular-season starting assignment are different facts. Camp attendance is not proof of a guaranteed contract or final roster place.

### Keep the evidence lanes separate

| Lane | What belongs here | What it can support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Individual drills | {{protocol, sample and results}} | Repeatability under those conditions |
| Practice / scrimmage | {{units, opponents, possessions and film}} | Execution in the observed situations |
| Preseason | {{closed game report; G, MPG and selected per-game figures}} | Actual preseason production and role use |
| Regular season | {{not started / actual closed report}} | Only regular-season evidence from games actually played |

Preseason and scrimmage totals never enter regular-season totals. Missing possessions or tracking data are not zero-valued performance.

## 5. If a trial is granted

| Trial detail | Actual agreement |
| --- | --- |
| Request | {{player's exact role/opportunity request and date}} |
| Staff decision | {{granted / modified / declined / awaiting; reason if communicated}} |
| Trial event | {{confirmed session/game and segment}} |
| Role during trial | {{responsibility; unit; matchup}} |
| Evaluation criteria | {{two or three observable tasks and denominator}} |
| Availability condition | {{staff-recorded participation limit}} |
| Review | {{time/event; evaluator; evidence needed}} |
| Outcome | {{not yet evaluated / observed result and next assignment}} |

A granted trial guarantees only that agreed opportunity, subject to recorded conditions. The coach still decides the rotation. A declined request can have a follow-up question without automatically producing a grievance, morale change or future trade request.
